The test image shows a detached plant stem on newspaper with:
- Dark, necrotic lesions/cankers on the stem
- Mixed green (healthy) and dark brown (diseased) stem tissue
- Withered/dead leaves attached at a node
- No visible white mold or fruiting bodies

This pattern points strongly to a stem canker disease. Let me view one reference image for Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers to confirm.

The reference for Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers shows concentrated black necrosis at the stem base/crown with roots, while the test image shows a detached upper stem section with dark brown necrotic lesions spanning a longer segment and dead leaves at a node.

The test image features dark, elongated stem canker lesions with withered/dead leaves attached — consistent with Alternaria stem canker appearing higher on the plant. The dark brown-to-black discoloration of the stem tissue matches Alternaria stem infection patterns.

{"prediction": "Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers", "confidence": 0.6, "reasoning": "Detached tomato stem showing dark brown/black necrotic stem lesions with dead, withered leaves at a node. The stem exhibits discrete canker-like discoloration typical of Alternaria stem infection, with green tissue remaining between lesioned areas. No white mycelium (rules out Sclerotinia/Southern Blight), no fruiting bodies, and the lesion pattern is on the stem rather than leaves, pointing to Alternaria stem canker."}
